content.title: City of Arvada Announces Decision Not to Proceed with W. 72nd Avenue Railroad Underpass
content.summary: The City of Arvada has decided not to proceed with the W. 72nd Avenue railroad underpass project due to a significant cost increase, with the latest estimate reaching approximately $137 million, more than double the original bond amount approved in 2018. City officials cited financial risks and the potential impact on other city services as key reasons for the decision, while exploring alternative improvements such as an at-grade crossing. A community open house is scheduled for February 2 to discuss the decision and gather input from residents.
content.body:
The City of Arvada will not move forward with construction of the roadway underpass at the railroad for the W. 72nd Avenue widening project from Kipling to Oak streets due to significant cost escalation.

The most recent cost estimate brings the project total to approximately $137 million, more than double the original $64.5 million bond amount approved by voters in 2018. Key cost drivers include a multi-year delay in approvals from the Union Pacific Railroad and the effects of extreme inflation in the transportation construction industry in the last five years. 

The most recent project estimate of $97.5 million had been incorporated into the City’s 10-year financial model. However, the new estimate, which included extensive negotiations with the contractor, prompted City leadership to reassess the project’s feasibility.

City Manager, Don Wick led the decision making process, “This decision was difficult, and our responsibility to the community requires us to be transparent about costs and make fiscally sound decisions. Our commitment must be to manage public funds responsibly and maintain the financial health of the City.”

The substantially higher costs would require significant redistribution of funds from other City services, possibly taking on additional debt, and could risk the City’s reserve funds. This would limit funds available for other capital projects, potentially affect operational budgets, and restrict the financial flexibility to respond to future community needs such as economic downturn or natural disaster recovery. Once construction begins, the City is obligated to finish the project. Given these financial risks and the complexity of underground work that could lead to additional project costs, the City determined it could not responsibly proceed with the underpass. 

Director of Infrastructure, Jacqueline Rhoades explained, “We remain committed to the original intent of the ballot measure to improve safety and traffic flow along the W. 72nd Avenue corridor. While the underpass is no longer feasible at this cost, we are actively exploring alternative improvements, including an at-grade crossing. We will keep the community informed as we continue evaluating improvements that are both effective and financially responsible.” 

In 2026, the City will restore existing conditions from Kipling to Oak streets, including repaving. For the long term, the City has begun to evaluate the feasibility and associated costs of an at-grade crossing and widening. 

Evaluating an at-grade crossing will take time to redesign, estimate costs, and receive approvals from the Union Pacific Railroad and Public Utilities Commission. At this early stage, the City estimates the redesign, approvals, and construction could take five to 10 years to complete. 

### Community Open House

The City will host a community open house on **Monday, Feb. 2, from 5-7 pm at the Apex Community Recreation Center****, 6842 Wadsworth Blvd.** Community members are invited to learn more about the decision, ask questions, and speak with City leaders and staff. The open house invites attendees to stop by at their convenience during the 2-hour window. There will not be a formal presentation, rather information will be shared in other formats. Information will be available digitally after the open house for those unable to attend. 

For more information, visit the [W. 72nd Avenue project webpage](/669).

### 2018 Voter Approved Bond Background

In the November 6, 2018 election, Arvada residents approved Ballot Issue 3F for a bond issue of $79.8 million to fund improvements to Ralston Road and W 72nd Avenue. The Ralston Road project began in 2021 and was completed in 2024 at a total cost of approximately $24 million. $41 million has been spent on W 72nd Avenue improvements including utility work, widening Simms Street to Oak Street and bike and pedestrian improvements.
